content:
Dating reality shows have always been a hugely popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into this space. Although their newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is effectively the streaming platform's first dating series.

"The Last Person on Earth" is hosted by renowned couples therapist Esther Perel, who will conduct an "innovative experiment"

Esther Perel is a celebrated couples therapist and New York Times bestselling author specialising in the field of human relationships.

Perel is also the central figure in Apple TV+'s newly announced 8-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth".

According to a press release: "In the series, seemingly mismatched couples will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of professional matchmakers and therapists, before embarking on a journey to one of the world's most romantic and remote destinations."

It sounds just like a reality show, but it sidesteps the baggage that comes with the "reality" brand. I suspect Apple is trying to give this dating series an air of "prestige" by labelling it a "documentary series".

The series has not yet announced a premiere date, but is expected to debut sometime in 2027.

It's also worth mentioning that Apple announced yesterday that it will adapt the latest romance novel from bestselling author Rebecca Yarros into a TV series. Clearly, the streaming platform is keen to expand its horizons beyond its existing core genres of sci-fi, comedy and thriller.

Apple TV+ costs US$12.99 per month, or you can get a discount through the Apple One bundle.
